classification.difficultyReason: Identify corresponding given sides and angles, select a standard congruence test and order the vertices.

content.prompt: In each part, write a congruence statement, giving a congruence test as the reason.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 7C question 2(a), bottom of printed page 197
spec.description: Two separate triangles side by side in different orientations; no right-angle marks. Decorative blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=3.5 cm, AC=2 cm, BC=4 cm; DF=2 cm, FE=3.5 cm, DE=4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All measurements and vertex labels are permanent question givens; no answer is shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}BA&=EF=3.5\text{ cm}\\AC&=FD=2\text{ cm}\\BC&=ED=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, so $\triangle BAC\equiv\triangle EFD$ (SSS).

spec.description: Paired separate triangles with the equal included angles labelled inside the lower vertices. Decorative blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AC=EF=3 cm, BC=DF=5 cm, angle ACB=angle EFD=100 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied sides, angles and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AC&=EF=3\text{ cm}\\CB&=FD=5\text{ cm}\\\angle ACB&=\angle EFD=100^\circ\end{align*}$$
Two corresponding sides and their included angles are equal, so $\triangle ACB\equiv\triangle EFD$ (SAS).

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(c), above question 3 on printed page 198
spec.description: Two separate triangles side by side; retain the differently oriented corresponding 6 cm sides and both given angles. Decorative blue outlines are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AC=ED=6 cm, angle BAC=angle FED=40 degrees, angle ACB=angle EDF=25 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the third angles and congruence statement are not printed in the question.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=\angle FED=40^\circ\\\angle ACB&=\angle EDF=25^\circ\\AC&=ED=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Two corresponding angles and a matching side are equal, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle EFD$ (AAS).
